basis: Craniofacial skeletal syndrome; intellectual disability/developmental delay in 7/19 (~37%). Hypospadias affects 4/19 overall (~21%); ocular and hearing abnormalities are below 30%.

decisions.renal: none: hypospadias occurs in 4/8 males but only 4/19 patients overall (~21%); common renal-axis involvement is not established.

basis: Defined by testicular maldevelopment, cryptorchidism, infertility and germ-cell cancer; endocrine dysfunction is not established by the disease definition.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: reproductive testicular dysgenesis does not establish hormonal dysfunction; the hypogonadism ancestor alone is insufficient.

basis: Exocrine pancreatic primary; liver metastases directly occupy and damage hepatic tissue in roughly 50% or more over the usual course.

decisions.hepatic: involved: liver metastases occur in roughly 50% or more over the course and represent spread of the same malignancy.

basis: Brainstem developmental abnormalities cause defining horizontal gaze palsy; progressive scoliosis defines skeletal involvement. Intrinsic ocular damage is not established as common.

decisions.ocular: none: horizontal gaze palsy reflects central brainstem dysfunction; isolated refractive findings in tiny samples do not establish common intrinsic eye disease.

basis: Ectodermal dysplasia; intellectual disability/seizures, aganglionic megacolon and vertebral abnormalities each occur in 80-99%; blepharophimosis omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability and seizures occur in 80-99%; the supplied classification establishes ectodermal disease as the primary site.

basis: Hypotonia, ataxia and abnormal auditory brainstem responses define neurologic dysfunction; nystagmus alone establishes neither intrinsic eye damage nor hearing loss.

decisions.ocular: none: congenital nystagmus can arise from central neurologic dysfunction; no independent ocular lesion or visual loss is established.

basis: Steroid metabolism disorder with defining severe hypertension. Nephrocalcinosis occurs in 30-79% as a separate complication; renal insufficiency occurs in 5-29%.

decisions.renal: none: nephrocalcinosis (30-79%) is a separately diagnosed complication; direct renal functional impairment is documented in only 5-29%.

basis: Postsynaptic neuromuscular junction dysfunction defines the disease; ophthalmoparesis and ptosis reflect junction failure, without established intrinsic ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: ophthalmoparesis and ptosis arise from neuromuscular junction dysfunction; their frequency does not establish direct eye or eyelid disease.

basis: Cardiac channelopathies are the predominant established presentation; neurologic and skeletal findings are subtype-dependent, with no evidence they affect most across this umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: none: neurodevelopmental disease is a distinct subtype; neurologic involvement is not established in most patients across the umbrella.

basis: Renal tubular reabsorption defect causes urinary glucose and glycine loss; the supplied evidence establishes renal transport dysfunction without a separate metabolic disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: glycosuria and hyperglycinuria establish abnormal renal reabsorption; an endocrine or intermediary metabolic defect is not demonstrated.
